description: The extended arm of 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, pinned at the fatal open call site. This case fixes WHICH of that paragraph's two arms runs and what the arm computes, byte by byte; case10 is the reference for the three-line abend tail the fatal arms share and records the mainframe-versus-translation status provenance. The two are read together and this one is not a second copy of it. REACHING THE ARM: the case declares no ACCTFILE input at all, which is how this contract states that the account master is not there to be opened - DatasetInput admits exactly one of "rows", "fixture" or "empty": true, and says in its own refusal that a dataset the case says nothing about must be omitted from "inputs" altogether. Omission is the only declaration in this harness that reaches a failing OPEN: a declared dataset is describable, so AccountRepository.open resolves its statements and reports '00', which is why a short row reaches the fatal READ arm (case13, case14) and a dataset that exists and holds no row reaches the first-read end-of-file arm (case03) instead. 0000-ACCTFILE-OPEN at app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl:L133-L149 then moves 8 into APPL-RESULT at L134, issues OPEN INPUT at L135, tests the status against '00' and nothing else at L136 so L139 moves 12, and fails the APPL-AOK guard at L141: DISPLAY 'ERROR OPENING ACCTFILE' at L144 - the bare DD name, and not ACCOUNT FILE as the read literal at L110 and the close literal at L162 are - then MOVE ACCTFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS at L145, PERFORM 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS at L146 and PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM at L147, which displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at L170, moves 0 into TIMING at L171 and 999 into ABCODE at L172, and calls 'CEE3ABD' at L173. ABCODE 999 and TIMING 0 are Language Environment abend parameters and are never the return code: the return code is 12, from the MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT at L139, carried out of the program by that call. WHICH ARM, AND WHY: the guard at L177-L178 is IF IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC OR IO-STAT1 = '9'. The status this run reports is AccountRepository.PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS, whose first byte is the CHARACTER '9' - US-ASCII 0x39 - and whose second byte is a RAW BINARY byte, 0x00, emphatically not the printable digit '0', which is 0x30. Both halves of the OR therefore hold here: 0x00 is not a digit, so the class condition IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC is true, and IO-STAT1 is '9' as well. This case consequently pins that the extended arm is taken, not which half of the OR selected it; the two halves are separated by FileStatusTest against the paragraph itself, where a numeric status such as '22' or '23' takes the other arm on a first byte that is not '9'. DERIVING THE FOUR-BYTE IMAGE, STATEMENT BY STATEMENT - the mechanism is reproduced exactly as written, REDEFINES trick included, because it is legacy behaviour and not a defect to modernise. 01 IO-STATUS-04 is IO-STATUS-0401 PIC 9 followed by IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999 at L57-L59, four bytes in all. (1) MOVE IO-STAT1 TO IO-STATUS-04(1:1) at L179 copies byte 1 of the status into byte 1 of the image verbatim, so the image opens with the character '9'. (2) MOVE 0 TO TWO-BYTES-BINARY at L180 clears the two-byte PIC 9(4) BINARY field declared at L53 to zero. (3) MOVE IO-STAT2 TO TWO-BYTES-RIGHT at L181 writes the raw status byte into the LOW-ORDER byte of that binary field, because 01 TWO-BYTES-ALPHA REDEFINES TWO-BYTES-BINARY at L54-L56 as TWO-BYTES-LEFT PIC X followed by TWO-BYTES-RIGHT PIC X; the high-order byte is still zero from step 2, so TWO-BYTES-BINARY now holds the UNSIGNED value of that byte, which for 0x00 is 0. (4) MOVE TWO-BYTES-BINARY TO IO-STATUS-0403 at L182 delivers that value to a PIC 999 receiver, which renders it zero-padded to exactly three digits: 000. (5) The image is therefore '9' followed by 000, and DISPLAY 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' IO-STATUS-04 at L183 concatenates the 20-character literal with those four bytes into a 24-character line, FILE STATUS IS: NNNN9000. The NNNN is part of the hard-coded literal at L183 and L187 and stays verbatim; it is not a placeholder awaiting substitution. THE RULE IS THE GENERAL ONE: because step 3 deposits an unsigned byte in 0..255 and step 4 pads to three digits, a second byte of x'04' renders 004 for an image of 9004, x'0A' renders 010 for 9010, and x'FF' renders 255 for 9255 - never a truncated 4, never a widened 0004, and never a negative number. FileStatus.toStatusImage is the Java home of the paragraph and FileStatusTest asserts exactly those boundaries - 0x00, 0x0A, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFF - against it. What this case may state as an OBSERVED line, however, is only the byte the translated backend actually reports. AccountRepository fixes its feedback byte at binary zero, on the stated ground that a refused operation carries no VSAM feedback code and inventing one would put a number into a job's log that no backend produced; and CBACT01CParityTest composes the expected status line for every case whose return code is not zero from FileStatus.toDisplayLine(AccountRepository.PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS). A case file asserting 9004 here would be asserting a byte that no code path in this module can produce, and making one produce it would mean editing that constant - outside this file's scope, and contradicting the constant's own reason for existing. The x'04' walkthrough is therefore recorded here rather than silently forced into the expectation, and the frozen 9000 is what is asserted. WHY THE LINE STILL DISCRIMINATES THE TWO ARMS: rendered through the numeric arm at L184-L187 this same status would give MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04 then MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2), which is 00 followed by '9' and the raw 0x00 - a 24-character line whose last byte is a NUL - while an implementation that simply hard-coded that arm's zero prefix would emit FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0000. Both differ from the expected line, so a translation that takes the wrong arm, or that reads the second byte as a character rather than as an unsigned binary value, fails this case instead of passing it. WHAT IS NOT HERE: nothing is read, so no labelled field line, no 49-hyphen separator and no 300-byte record image appears; L173 terminates the program before the closing banner at L85, so the END OF EXECUTION line appears nowhere; SYSOUT is exactly these four lines, of 38, 22, 24 and 16 characters. Nothing is written anywhere - the empty expectedWrites asserts that positively - and no dataset survives the run to have a final state reported for it, so expectedFinalState is empty too. No job parameter is declared, because app/jcl/READACCT.jcl:L22 is a bare EXEC PGM=CBACT01C with no PARM. No normalisation is declared, because no fixture is seeded. No fully-qualified dataset name appears: a case addresses a dataset by binding key alone, and the key this program uses is ACCTFILE, declared at app/jcl/READACCT.jcl:L25. Every expected line is US-ASCII - the code page of app/data/ASCII and of ParityHarness.FIXTURE_CHARSET - and never a platform default. The case is deterministic: it carries no wall-clock and no random value, and the condition it forces is the absence of the input rather than anything computed, so repeated runs produce the same four lines. PROVENANCE: statically derived by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl, cross-checked against app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy for the 300-byte record this run never reaches and app/jcl/READACCT.jcl for the DD and the absent PARM, and against the constants published by AccountBalanceJob, AbendException, AccountRepository and FileStatus. Nothing here was captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler as disabled, and no Language Environment CEE service exists to link the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at L173. That substitution of provenance, and nothing else about the gate, is the escalated deviation recorded as risk R-A. No user rules were provided for this project, so this fixture is held to the enterprise practices instead - real and exact strings, read-only legacy sources, the mechanism preserved as written, determinism, explicitly named code page and byte semantics, a step-by-step derivation, and an environmental limit documented rather than absorbed.
